crm_notes:
Summary:
- Vertical: mid-to-large healthcare payer/provider; high sensitivity to PHI and retention/residency rules.
- Primary ask: private inference (VPC/on-prem) + audit logging + KMS. Latency SLA ~ <150ms p95 for chat, throughput ~ 30 qps. Cost-sensitive but willing to commit for data residency/ISO guarantees.
Security review specifics:
- InfoSec team requires SOC2 Type II report and ISO27001 certificate plus evidence of continuous pen testing.
- They explicitly declined to share third-party vendor SOC2 reports with Redwood (internal policy: no outbound vendor evidence). Quote from CTO Priya Rao: "We can't provide raw SOC reports across vendors — our procurement will only move if vendor can present ISO attestation + legal addendum."
- Redwood offered alternative paths: signed NDA + on-prem inspection, SOC2 bridge letter, SCCs + contract clauses, or private deployment with AES-HSM keys. Aurelia rejected each due to internal compliance policy and timeline.
POC notes:
- POC ran for 3 weeks on dedicated nodes; performance hit targets but was never promoted to contract stage because security gating blocked access to production data for validation.
Commercial motion:
- Pricing discussed and modeled (estimated ARR $200k-$500k). Legal/Procurement sent draft SLA but procurement deprioritized due to FY26 budget reshuffle.
Outcome / Recommended action:
- Mark as closed-lost: primary reason = security review failed (SOC2/ISO evidence gap + unwillingness to share). Secondary factors: competitor offering ISO attestation, budget freeze, loss of internal champion.
- Next: send formal exit note, include summary of mitigation options offered, keep on a 6-month re-engagement cadence in case policies change or they request private on-prem package.
- Store Infosec Q&A and POC perf logs under SUP-4821 / SEC-9202 for reference.
